# `laws`

**Enacted laws**

One row per enacted law the Congress.gov law list route states, with the Statutes at Large citation from the law's own PLAW USLM file where captured. Keyed on the law's Congress, type and number, not on the bill; `bill_id` is the foreign key to `congress_bills`, whose `statutes_at_large_cite` the host fills from this table at that table's merge. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

**Coverage.** Sampled. Measured on one cold-start run (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`): `law/119` declared 108 and served 108 on one page for one keyed request, and all 108 became rows; the PLAW leg spent 108 keyless requests under its 300-per-run cap and established 102 Statutes at Large citations. The Congress.gov law route for the scoped Congresses (the current one by default) is walked whole each run and every law it lists is a row; the PLAW USLM citation is added per law, newest first, under the per-run cap. A steady-state run is meant to ask only about laws whose list row moved or whose PLAW the bulk folder had not yet served. **The skip is design, not measurement**: D1 was a cold start, so nothing was held and nothing was skipped, and the saving described here has not been observed yet — the second run is what measures it. *(measured 2026-09-19)*

**Data quality.** `statutes_at_large_cite` is set when `uslm_outcome` is `captured`; read every NULL through `uslm_outcome` and `uslm_reason`. `unavailable` (reason `source_unavailable`) is the publisher's own lag, a `404` from the exact PLAW locator: on 2026-09-19 the route listed 108 laws and the PLAW bulk folder held 104, the four newest (119-103, 119-104, 119-109, 119-110) absent; each is retried every run until the folder serves it.
`captured_partial` is a validated USLM file that states no Statutes at Large citation (reason `statutes_citation_not_stated`): the two private laws of the 119th (`PLAW-119pvtl1`, `PLAW-119pvtl2`), whose own `citableAs` values are kept in `uslm_citable_as_json`. Until reader rule `laws-uslm-v2` (2026-09-25) the contract refused those two files and their rows said `not_requested`, although both were requested and served. `captured_refused` keeps the digest of a `200` body the reader refused, either another law's file (`native_identity_refused`) or not native USLM at all, such as an HTML page (`native_shape_refused`), and none of its unvalidated fields. `request_failed` is an attempted read that established nothing, a transport failure included; it is never published as `unavailable`. `not_requested` means only that no request was made, which the per-run cap decides.
A validated row (`captured` or `captured_partial`) is not re-read unless its list row's `update_date` moves or `uslm_reader_version` changes, and a failed later attempt never replaces it. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

- **Parquet file:** `laws.parquet`
- **MCP `query_sql` support:** Configured; requires an available artifact.
- **Publication status:** Not established by this schema page or its measurement date.

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `law_id` | `VARCHAR` | Natural key: congress, law_type and number joined with hyphens. |
| `congress` | `VARCHAR` | The numbered Congress that enacted the law. |
| `law_type` | `VARCHAR` | `public` or `private`: the publisher's Public Law or Private Law folded onto the spelling the PLAW USLM publicPrivate field uses, so the list route, the bulk folder and the USLM file share one key. |
| `number` | `VARCHAR` | The law's number within its Congress and type, without the Congress prefix. |
| `law_number` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's own spelling of the number, Congress prefix included. |
| `publisher_law_type` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's laws[].type exactly as spelled (Public Law or Private Law). |
| `package_id` | `VARCHAR` | The GovInfo PLAW package id by the measured bulk-file rule: `PLAW-` plus congress, publ or pvtl, and number. |
| `bill_id` | `VARCHAR` | Natural key of the measure this law enacted, as congress_bills keys it. |
| `bill_type` | `VARCHAR` | The enacted measure's type, lowercased as the bill tables spell it. |
| `bill_number` | `VARCHAR` | The enacted measure's number. |
| `title` | `VARCHAR` | The measure's title as the list route states it. |
| `origin_chamber` | `VARCHAR` | The chamber the measure originated in, as the publisher states it. |
| `origin_chamber_code` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's one-letter origin chamber code. |
| `latest_action_date` | `VARCHAR` | Date of the publisher's latestAction entry, which for a law is the became-law action. |
| `latest_action_text` | `VARCHAR` | Text of that latestAction entry. |
| `update_date` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's updateDate on the list row; the merge prefers the larger value. |
| `update_date_including_text` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's updateDateIncludingText on the list row. |
| `url` | `VARCHAR` | The publisher's own URL for the enacted measure. |
| `statutes_at_large_cite` | `VARCHAR` | The native Statutes at Large citation, when stated. NULL with captured_partial means the acquired identity-matched USLM does not state this citation; see uslm_reason and uslm_citable_as_json. |
| `statutes_at_large_volume` | `VARCHAR` | The volume part of that citation. |
| `statutes_at_large_page` | `VARCHAR` | The page part of that citation. |
| `approved_date` | `VARCHAR` | The USLM meta's approvedDate, where the PLAW was captured. |
| `uslm_title` | `VARCHAR` | The USLM meta's dc:title, where the PLAW was captured. |
| `uslm_processed_date` | `VARCHAR` | The USLM meta's processedDate, where the PLAW was captured. |
| `uslm_sha256` | `VARCHAR` | Digest of the captured PLAW USLM bytes, so the citation is traceable to one file. |
| `uslm_observed_at` | `VARCHAR` | When the PLAW USLM was captured. |
| `uslm_outcome` | `VARCHAR` | captured or captured_partial retain validated native metadata; captured_refused retains a refused capture without unvalidated metadata; request_failed records an attempted read without an accepted body; unavailable records supported source absence; not_requested means no attempt. |
| `uslm_citable_as_json` | `VARCHAR` | Every literal native USLM meta citableAs value, source order retained. |
| `uslm_reason` | `VARCHAR` | Bounded outcome reason token; NULL on complete capture or when no read was attempted. |
| `uslm_reader_version` | `VARCHAR` | Native mapping rule used for this attempted read; old or absent rules require rereading. |
